chunk_findings.detail: The added regression test asserts `merge_log(tmp_path) == [main_sha]`, but `merge_log` is implemented with `git log ... --format=%H %s` and returns the full log lines, not bare SHAs; the existing test at the end of the file demonstrates this by extracting subjects from those returned lines. In the new repository the merge subject is `merge T1: real`, so `merge_log(tmp_path)` returns `["<main_sha> merge T1: real"]`, not `[main_sha]`, causing both assertions in the new test to fail even after the intended fix. The test should compare against the full `"%H %s"` line or split the SHA out of the returned entries.

chunk_findings.detail: `merge_log` now invokes `git log main ...` and then treats any nonzero exit as “no merges” (`return []`). In a common branch/CI checkout there may be no local `main` ref at all—only `origin/main`—or the clone may be `--single-branch`. Then `git log main` fails with “unknown revision”, `merge_log` returns `[]`, the recall test sees `total == 0`, and calls `pytest.skip("too few replayable merges...")`. The new regression guard therefore silently skips instead of checking main’s recent merges, so the B2822f97531 regression can pass unguarded in exactly the branch-checkout environment the change is meant to fix.

chunk_findings.detail: `blind` is built from `residual` across all results before `unexpected` is computed, and then `unexpected` drops every `lost` test whose ID appears blind anywhere. A test that has one blind loss and one normal, non-blind loss is therefore removed from `unexpected` even though the normal loss is a fresh selector miss that must fail the test. Example: results = [(m1, 0, ["a"], ["a (blind: timeout)"]), (m2, 0, ["a"], ["a"])] gives `blind={"a"}` and `unexpected=[]`, hiding the m2 regression.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_recall.py:246,252

chunk_findings.detail: `merge_log` anchors to `main` only when a local `refs/heads/main` resolves; otherwise it silently falls back to `HEAD`. In a PR CI checkout that leaves HEAD detached and has only `origin/main` (no local `main`), `git rev-parse --verify main` fails, so the window still walks the branch tip and the branch-history dependence from B2822f97531 remains. The comment says the fallback is for a renamed default branch, but the code cannot distinguish that case from the remote-only main case.
